name: Ironforge Airfield
summary: High above Dun Morogh, gnome flying machines and dwarven mountaineers hold a remote airfield northeast of Ironforge. Its plateau overlooks jagged crags and the steep descent toward the Wetlands.

sections.title: A Hidden Redoubt in the Crags
sections.body: High above Dun Morogh's trails, gnome flying machines line open landing strips among the mountain peaks. Dwarven masonry anchors the ridgelines, and mountaineers watch the perimeter. Nearby, engineers tend the machines and inspect their engines in the cold.

sections.title: Frontier Skirmishes and Frozen Valleys
sections.body: The valley around the airfield is contested ground. Frostmane trolls dwell in nearby caves and harass the dwarven sentries. Across frozen waters beneath the peaks, dwarven defenders and Stormpike patrols clash with troll raiders, keeping the outpost on guard.

faq.q: How do you get up to the airfield?
faq.answer: No roads, flights, or maintained tunnels connect the valley to Ironforge or lower Dun Morogh. You must climb the steep mountainsides on foot, following difficult ridgeline paths from Loch Modan or near Dun Morogh's passes.

faq.q: What is the purpose of this place?
faq.answer: The airfield is a high outpost for testing and maintaining flying machines, and for scouting the mountain borderlands between Dun Morogh, Loch Modan, and the Wetlands. Dwarven mountaineers and gnome engineers work there.

faq.q: Who is attacking the dwarven guards here?
aliases: who is fighting on the lake
faq.answer: Frostmane trolls from nearby caves attack the dwarven guards. The mountaineers clash with them over the frozen lake below the runway.

faq.q: Is the airfield tied to any official quests?
faq.answer: No standard assignment sends travelers to the airstrip. The remote plateau lies apart from the dwarven kingdom's main routes.

angles.text: For a tinker, the airstrip shows gnomish flying machines assembled and kept in extreme cold.
As a dwarf, you know Ironforge's Mountaineers keep watch even in Khaz Modan's most inaccessible heights.
